awareness.title: What PCOD actually is
awareness.paragraph1: PCOD (Polycystic Ovarian Disorder) is a hormonal condition that affects how the ovaries work. It's common — estimates suggest it touches roughly 1 in 5 women in India — and it shows up differently in everyone: irregular periods, weight changes, acne, or excess hair growth are all possible signs.
awareness.paragraph2: There's no single test that confirms it on the spot. Doctors usually piece together symptoms, a physical exam, and sometimes bloodwork or an ultrasound. RutuChakra doesn't replace that process — it looks at patterns in your symptoms the same way a first conversation with a doctor might, and gives you a clearer picture of whether it's worth following up.

form.subtitle: A gentle 4-step symptom check to raise awareness about PCOS & PCOD. No lab tests — just your lived experience.

section1.title: Let's start with the basics
section1.desc: Enter your age, weight, and height. BMI is calculated automatically — no math needed.
section1.infoBox: BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height² (m). It is one of several indicators — not a standalone measure of PCOS risk or overall health.

section2.title: Your cycle pattern
section2.desc: Drag the slider to select your average menstrual cycle length. Regularity is determined automatically from the value you choose.
section2.infoBox: Your regularity is decided automatically. A typical cycle is 21–35 days. Cycles shorter, longer, absent, or very unpredictable may signal a hormonal imbalance.

section3.title: What have you been experiencing?
section3.desc: Select every symptom that applies. These are self-reportable — no tests needed. Tap to select or deselect.
section3.infoBox: Even one or two symptoms can be worth discussing with a doctor. PCOS presents differently in every person.

section4.title: Your everyday routine
section4.desc: Diet and activity directly affect insulin resistance and hormone levels — both key factors in PCOS.
section4.fastFoodQuestion: Do you consume fast food frequently?
section4.infoBox: A sedentary lifestyle and diet high in processed food can worsen hormonal imbalance and elevate PCOS risk over time.
